r0.why: First of three Phanerozoic eras [1]; 538.8 to 251.902 Ma after Neoproterozoic [2]; six periods in order [3]; informal early/late split [4].

r1.why: Greek 'ancient life' [7]; Sedgwick 1838 for Cambrian and Ordovician [5]; Phillips 1840 Cambrian to Permian [6].

r2.why: 'Its first period held the Cambrian explosion' is not supported: none of the cited sentences [8],[9],[10],[11],[40] says the Cambrian is the first period of the Paleozoic (that is in uncited [3]).

r3.why: Major division [16]; Sedgwick's trilobite-based base [17]; SSF markers [18]; skeletal fossils rarely preserved in most sequences [19]; ICS trace fossils [20]; reflect body-plan complexity [22],[24].

r4.why: Two decades, Fortune Head GSSP at base of Treptichnus pedum assemblage [25]; 538.8 +/- 0.6 Ma, below trilobites and SSF [26].

r5.why: Pannotia breakup at start [33]; Iapetus and sea-level rise [34]; Gondwana 510 Ma [36]; Acadian-Caledonian uplifts [37]; Pangaea and mountain chains [38].

r6.why: Ended with P-T, largest of Phanerozoic [13]; 30 Myr land recovery, sea faster [14],[15]; Hindeodus parvus [27]; Meishan GSSP [31]; 251.902 +/- 0.024 Ma from clay layers [32].
